skill_markdown:
# Trio Analysis Tutorial

## Overview

This workflow performs a comprehensive trio analysis using synthetic datasets sourced from the [RD-Connect GPAP](https://rd-connect.eu/). It is designed to identify causative genetic variants by analyzing the genomic data of an affected individual alongside their parents. The process begins by retrieving authorized VCF datasets using the [EGA Download Client](https://github.com/EGA-archive/pyega3), followed by text processing and filtering to isolate specific case files.

The pipeline includes several critical data preparation steps, such as decompressing files, fixing headers, and standardizing chromosome nomenclature via regex. It utilizes [bcftools](https://samtools.github.io/bcftools/) for variant normalization and filtering—specifically removing `<NON_REF>` alleles—before merging individual samples into a single multi-sample VCF.

Once merged, variants are annotated using [SnpEff](https://pcingola.github.io/SnpEff/) to predict functional impacts. The workflow then leverages the [GEMINI](https://gemini.readthedocs.io/) framework to load the annotated variants into a database and query for specific inheritance patterns, such as de novo or autosomal recessive mutations. For final interpretation, the results are integrated with [gene.iobio](https://gene.iobio.io/) for real-time visual prioritization of candidate genes.

## Inputs and data preparation

| Step | Label | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | pedigree | data_input |  |


Ensure your pedigree file is in PED format and that all input VCFs are correctly normalized and merged before loading into GEMINI. When handling large-scale trio data, organizing your VCF files into a dataset collection can significantly streamline the normalization and annotation steps. For automated testing and job configuration, you can use `planemo workflow_job_init` to generate a `job.yml` file. Detailed instructions on data acquisition from EGA and specific pedigree formatting requirements are available in the README.md. Always verify that chromosome naming conventions are consistent across all input files to prevent errors during the merge process.

## How to run (Planemo)

### Local Galaxy (default engine)

```bash
planemo run main_workflow.ga job.yml --download_outputs --output_directory . --output_json output.json
```

Optional: `--galaxy_root /path/to/galaxy` speeds up spinning up a local Galaxy.

### Docker Galaxy

Append e.g. `--engine docker_galaxy --ignore_dependency_problems` (requires Docker).

### External Galaxy (usegalaxy.org / EU / …)

```bash
planemo run main_workflow.ga job.yml --engine external_galaxy --galaxy_url SERVER_URL --galaxy_user_key YOUR_API_KEY
```

Create a reusable profile: `planemo profile_create myprofile --galaxy_url ... --galaxy_user_key ... --engine external_galaxy` then `planemo run main_workflow.ga job.yml --profile myprofile`.

### Job file

- Generate a template: `planemo workflow_job_init main_workflow.ga -o job.yml`
- Lint: `planemo workflow_lint main_workflow.ga`

See **[Running Galaxy workflows](https://planemo.readthedocs.io/en/master/running.html)** in the Planemo documentation.

## Invocation outputs

After a successful run with `--download_outputs`, files appear under your chosen `--output_directory`. `--output_json` records CWL-style metadata for outputs (paths, checksums).

On an external Galaxy, use `planemo invocation_download INVOCATION_ID --profile ...` to fetch outputs, or track progress with `planemo workflow_track INVOCATION_ID`.

Workflow steps marked as **workflow outputs** in the editor are listed under **Workflow outputs**; exact filenames depend on tools and Galaxy configuration.

## Files

- `main_workflow.ga` — Galaxy workflow export (JSON)
- `job.yml` — inputs/parameters for `planemo run` (create with `planemo workflow_job_init`)
- [Planemo: Running Galaxy workflows](https://planemo.readthedocs.io/en/master/running.html)
